title: Eagles Stun Cowboys 39-38 in Thrilling Thanksgiving Comeback Victory
body:
Philadelphia staged one of the most dramatic turnarounds in recent NFL history on Thanksgiving night, erasing a 21‑point deficit to edge Dallas 39‑38 in a game that will be replayed in highlight reels for years. After trailing 31‑10 midway through the third quarter, the Eagles unleashed a relentless offensive surge while the Cowboys’ defense collapsed, culminating in a last‑second field goal by veteran kicker Jake Elliott that sealed the upset and left the Dallas crowd in stunned silence.

The Cowboys appeared to have the game in hand early. Dallas quarterback Dak Prescott connected on a 45‑yard strike to CeeDee Lamb, followed by a 22‑yard touchdown run by Ezekiel Elliott that pushed the lead to 21‑0. A quick field goal and a short rushing TD later, Dallas stretched the advantage to 31‑10, prompting many analysts to predict a comfortable victory for the home team. Yet the Eagles, playing under the bright lights of AT&T Stadium, refused to accept defeat. After a quick three‑and‑out, Philadelphia’s offense, orchestrated by quarterback Jalen Hurts, began to chip away at the margin with a mix of scrambles, play‑action passes and a revitalized ground game.

The comeback ignited in the fourth quarter when Hurts, having already thrown for 280 yards, found wide receiver A.J. Brown on a slant that resulted in a 34‑yard touchdown, narrowing the gap to 31‑17. The momentum shift was palpable; Dallas’ defense, which had been dominant for most of the night, appeared fatigued and out of sync. On the ensuing drive, the Eagles capitalized on a forced fumble, converting it into a short field goal that made it 31‑20. With just over five minutes remaining, Hurts engineered a methodical drive, culminating in a 12‑yard touchdown pass to DeVonta Smith, pulling the Eagles within three points at 31‑27.

Dallas responded with a field goal, extending the lead to 34‑27, but the Eagles struck again on the next possession. A daring fourth‑down conversion kept the drive alive, and a subsequent 7‑yard rush by Miles Sanders gave Philadelphia the lead for the first time, 34‑31. The Cowboys, now under pressure, managed a quick touchdown pass to Michael Gallup, reclaiming a 38‑34 advantage with less than two minutes left. However, the Eagles’ special teams unit delivered the decisive blow. After a disciplined drive that consumed precious seconds, Jake Elliott slotted a 48‑yard field goal as time expired, sending the visiting fans into a frenzy and handing Philadelphia a 39‑38 victory.

The outcome reverberates beyond the scoreboard. For the Eagles, the win bolsters their playoff aspirations, showcasing resilience and depth that had been questioned after a slow start to the season. Hurts’ poise under pressure, coupled with the offensive line’s improved protection, suggests a team capable of overcoming early setbacks. Conversely, the Cowboys must confront glaring defensive lapses, particularly in late‑game stamina and coverage breakdowns that allowed Philadelphia to exploit mismatches. Head coach Mike McCarthy’s decision to keep Prescott in the game despite a lingering shoulder injury also drew scrutiny, as the quarterback’s accuracy waned during the critical final drive.

Analysts will likely point to the Eagles’ adjustments at halftime—shifting to a more balanced attack and increasing the tempo—as the catalyst for the comeback. Meanwhile, Dallas’ inability to force a turnover after the third quarter highlights a missed opportunity to stifle Philadelphia’s resurgence. The game also underscores the growing parity in the NFC East, where any team can overturn a substantial lead with strategic play‑calling and execution.

Looking ahead, both franchises face pivotal matchups that could define their seasons. Philadelphia travels to face the New York Giants next week, a contest that will test whether the Eagles can sustain their newfound momentum against a disciplined defense. Dallas, on the other hand, returns home to host the Washington Commanders, where a swift response will be essential to restore confidence among a fan base still reeling from the Thanksgiving collapse. Regardless of the outcomes, the 39‑38 thriller will be remembered as a testament to the NFL’s unpredictability and the enduring allure of comeback football.
